claims.text: Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that it was encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that the screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) in a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
By default, this "photographic memory" captured sensitive content visible on screen—including passwords and private messages—and made it accessible to any process running as the user [Source: ev-1].
In response to these concerns, Microsoft delayed the feature initially announced on May 20, 2024 [Source: ev-1], and subsequently reversed its design.
While this revised version reached general availability in 2025, the initial controversy established it as a major privacy crisis for AI-powered PCs [Source: ev-1].
